data.title: Dolné Vestenice – a newly discovered Slavic hillfort
data.excerpt: A Slavic hillfort unknown until a few years ago was discovered in hard-to-reach terrain above the Hradištnica valley at Dolné Vestenice, and excavated by the Institute of Archaeology of the Slovak Academy of Sciences under Karol Pieta with the participation of the Hradiská civic association. On an area of about 0.5 ha it has yielded evidence of jewellers, metal casters and smiths, who among other things made axe-shaped currency bars.

children.text: A few years ago archaeologists discovered a hitherto unknown Slavic hillfort in the village of Dolné Vestenice. The Institute of Archaeology of the Slovak Academy of Sciences subsequently carried out an archaeological excavation here under the direction of Karol Pieta, in which the Hradiská civic association also took part. The hillfort lies in hard-to-reach terrain on the boundary of Dolné Vestenice and Uhrovské Podhradie, above the Hradištnica valley.

It is elongated in shape and occupies an area of approximately 0.5 ha. Its earliest occupation is attested in the Middle La Tène period and in the Migration Period. The largest and most important assemblage of finds, however, comes from the Early Middle Ages, from the 9th–10th centuries, that is to say from the period when Great Moravia existed.

The slopes of the hillfort are very steep and the whole site looks almost like a table mountain. Comfortable access was possible only partly from the north, where our ancestors built a massive rampart. The original entrance to the hillfort was evidently in these parts as well. In the other parts of the hillfort a timber palisade was sufficient as a fortification.

Matej Ruttkay states in the book Bojná 2 that traces of local production by various craftsmen – jewellers, metal casters, smiths and so on – were identified here. This is attested above all by the large number of semi-finished products. Karol Pieta adds that, within the intensive smithing production, the manufacture of axe-shaped currency bars, for example, is attested here. The most notable finds from the area of the hillfort include spurs with hooks, fragments of mail armour, lead ingots and models of earrings, a fragment of a lead cross, iron spurs with a long segmented spike, and arrowheads. Besides metal objects, a quantity of typical Slavic pottery with wavy-line decoration and parts of stone querns were found. The situation might indicate that the hillfort came to an end at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries.

children.text:
More stray finds and also hoards of currency bars and tools were found at the foot of the hillfort and in the wider surroundings. As in the area of Bojná, here too the occupation concentrates in mountain locations, where relatively high-lying mountain ridges were used as lines of communication. It seems that the reason for occupying upland sites in the Nitra region was, as in other historical phases, the unsettled times and the need to secure communities against sudden raids, perhaps combined with the control of strategic mountain passes and with the exploitation of the local ore wealth and of other natural resources, which is also archaeologically attested in the upper Nitra area.
Orgoň
